  <name>Task 2: pdflib.js lazy loader + resolver, verified against the real UMD in a vm sandbox</name>
  <files>site/js/app/pdflib.js, tests/js/pdflib.test.js</files>
  <behavior>
    - resolvePdfLib({ jspdf: { jsPDF: F }, autoTable: fn }) returns { jsPDF: F, autoTable: fn }
    - resolvePdfLib({ jspdf: { jsPDF: F } }) where F.API.autoTable is a function returns autoTable = (doc, opts) => doc.autoTable(opts) (calls through, returns undefined like the function form)
    - resolvePdfLib({ jspdf: { jsPDF: F }, applyPlugin: ap }) with no autoTable anywhere calls ap(F) once, then resolves via F.API.autoTable
    - resolvePdfLib({}) / missing jsPDF / missing autotable returns null (never throws)
    - Real UMD: a vm context with window/self/globalThis = the context (no module, no exports, no define) that runs jspdf.umd.min.js then jspdf.plugin.autotable.min.js as classic scripts yields resolvePdfLib(context) !== null; with that result, `new jsPDF({orientation:'landscape',unit:'pt',format:'a4'})` + autoTable(doc, {head:[['a']], body:[['b']]}) sets doc.lastAutoTable.finalY > 0
  </behavior>
  <action>
Create `site/js/app/pdflib.js` (LF line endings; header comment "Lazy loader for the vendored PDF libraries. resolvePdfLib is pure; loadPdfLib touches the DOM only when called."):
- `export const PDF_SCRIPTS = ['vendor/jspdf/jspdf.umd.min.js', 'vendor/jspdf-autotable/jspdf.plugin.autotable.min.js'];` (relative to index.html; order matters: jsPDF first).
- `export function resolvePdfLib(g)`: `const jsPDF = g && g.jspdf && g.jspdf.jsPDF;` if not a function return null. Then in order: (a) `typeof g.autoTable === 'function'` -> use it; (b) `jsPDF.API && typeof jsPDF.API.autoTable === 'function'` -> wrapper `(doc, opts) => { doc.autoTable(opts); }`; (c) `typeof g.applyPlugin === 'function'` -> call `g.applyPlugin(jsPDF)` then retry (b); else null. Wrap in try/catch -> null.
- `export function loadPdfLib(doc = globalThis.document, g = globalThis)`: memoised promise. If `resolvePdfLib(g)` already non-null, resolve with it. Else inject each `PDF_SCRIPTS` entry sequentially as a classic `<script src>` (create element, `async = false`, append to `doc.head`, resolve on `load`, reject `new Error('pdf_lib_unavailable')` on `error`), then `resolvePdfLib(g)`; null -> reject same error. On any rejection clear the memo so a later click can retry. Do not use `import(`, `fetch(` or `XMLHttpRequest` (static guards). Use `globalThis` (not the bare identifier `window`) so the module stays import-safe in node.

Create `tests/js/pdflib.test.js` (node:test, LF):
- Resolver cases from <behavior> with fake objects (F as a plain function with `F.API = {}`; record calls).
- Real-UMD test: `import vm from 'node:vm'`, read both vendor files with `readFileSync(repoUrl(...),'utf8')` (helpers.js `repoUrl`). Build `const ctx = vm.createContext({ console, TextEncoder, TextDecoder, atob, btoa, setTimeout, clearTimeout, URL, Blob, Uint8Array, ArrayBuffer })`, then `vm.runInContext('var window = this; var self = this; var globalThis = this;', ctx)` and run jspdf then autotable with `vm.runInContext(src, ctx, { filename })`. Log `Object.keys(ctx).filter(k => /pdf|auto|plugin/i.test(k))` with `t.diagnostic(...)` so the SUMMARY records the actual global names. Assert `resolvePdfLib(ctx)` non-null and that it can produce a 1-row table (behavior above). If jsPDF itself cannot initialise inside the vm (missing host API), add the missing global to the context rather than skipping; only if impossible, fall back to running the autotable UMD alone against a stub `ctx.jspdf = { jsPDF: function S(){} }` with `S.API = {}` and assert which global(s) appear — and record that fallback in the SUMMARY.
Record the observed global name(s) and which resolver branch the browser will hit in the SUMMARY (this closes research Open Question 1; the browser checkpoint in 15-06 re-confirms).
  </action>
